claims.text: A W-Ti-V-Cr refractory high-entropy alloy can be used as a low-activation structural material for high-temperature plasma-facing components in fusion reactors.
W, Ti, V, and Cr constitute a composition optimized for low activation.
The proposed W-Ti-V-Cr HEA has excellent high-temperature mechanical properties.
The proposed W-Ti-V-Cr HEA has irradiation resistance suitable for fusion-reactor service.
The W-Ti-V-Cr HEA may be used in either polycrystalline or single-crystal form.
Replacing high-activation elements with low-activation elements optimizes the HEA for low activation.
The proposed material is intended to operate at temperatures up to 1000°C under fusion-reactor irradiation.
Grain-boundary structure and composition mediate the effects of composition optimization.
The optimized HEA composition reduces the formation of high-activation phases.
The optimized HEA composition enhances grain-boundary stability.
Enhanced grain-boundary stability improves irradiation resistance.
Reduced formation of high-activation phases produces lower activation.
The optimized HEA will reduce activation level by 30% relative to traditional PFC alloys.
The optimized HEA will improve high-temperature yield strength and creep resistance by 20% relative to traditional PFC alloys.
Tungsten and stainless steel are traditional alloys used in current plasma-facing components.
The optimized HEA must have an activation level below 0.1% of the total composition.
The optimized HEA must retain its high-temperature mechanical properties after irradiation.

contradictions.description: The initial state permits a single crystal, while the proposed mediator and mechanism rely on grain-boundary structure and stability; a conventional single crystal lacks the grain-boundary network required by that mechanism.

The predicted outcome is a 20% improvement in mechanical properties, but the falsification rule refers to a reduction in those properties of less than 10%. This reverses the direction of the predicted effect and could classify limited degradation as falsifying even though it is preferable to greater degradation.
